clue.text: Heavy work by journalists given without limits

parts.note: op is the standard short form of opus, a musical work
the press is the collective name for journalists

indicators.note: losing its limits means the word given keeps only its inner letters, its first and last dropped

explanation.surface: A demanding piece of writing produced by reporters, offered with no restrictions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without limits' strips G and N from 'given', leaving IVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy can mean burdensome and harsh, as in a heavy regime, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Expel leaders of Oxford University student theatre

indicators.note: the leaders of these four words are their opening letters, taken in order

explanation.surface: Throw out the people in charge of a college drama society.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel someone is to force them out, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Attendant concealing crime in church home

indicators.note: concealing means the first word holds the second hidden inside it

parts.note: a page is a young attendant, for instance at a wedding or court
arson, deliberate fire-raising, is a crime

explanation.surface: A servant hides an offence inside a place of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman's house, provided by the church, is a home of this kind.

clue.text: Choose treat celebrity rejected in part

indicators.note: rejected says the hidden letters are read backwards
in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Pick a famous person to be partly snubbed after a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in part' lifts TCELE from 'treat celebrity'; 'rejected' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To choose is to pick or vote for, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Throw over a penny for youngster

indicators.note: over means the throw word is placed over, round, the two small pieces

parts.note: to sling is to throw
p is the abbreviation for a penny in British money

explanation.surface: Toss a coin across to a child.
explanation.definitionFit: A young tree is a youngster in the forest; the word is also used figuratively for a young person.

clue.text: Six fast to embrace love that's intense

indicators.note: to embrace means the first pieces wrap round the next one

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
Lent is the Christian period of fasting
love means zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Half a dozen rush to hug a loved one with great passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Something violent is extremely forceful, so intense works as a synonym.

clue.text: Ducks haircuts

definitions.meaning: ducks as a verb means dips or bends down quickly
short, even hairstyles at chin level

explanation.definitionFit: Ducking and bobbing are both quick downward movements, and a bob is also a classic short haircut.

clue.text: Oscar with lodge in tree

parts.note: Oscar is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for O
to lodge somewhere is to live there

explanation.surface: An Oscar winner stays up in a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The olive is a Mediterranean fruit tree, an example of the class.

clue.text: Second lawsuit including name editor authorised

indicators.note: including means the lawsuit word takes the next letter inside it

parts.note: an action is a legal case or lawsuit

explanation.surface: A second legal case naming an editor has been approved.
explanation.definitionFit: Something authorised has official permission, the same meaning as approved or sanctioned.

clue.text: Wrong user suffering agonies

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

indicators.note: suffering means the letters of user are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A mistreated drug user is in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Tortures are extreme pains, so agonies is a plural synonym.

clue.text: Hospital medic, not working, getting rise

indicators.note: not tells us to take the working word out of the medic

parts.note: a surgeon is a doctor working in a hospital
on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: A hospital doctor off duty is getting a pay increase.
explanation.definitionFit: A surge is a sudden increase, so it matches rise as a noun.

clue.text: In favour of proposal for marketing

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a motion is a proposal put to a meeting

explanation.surface: Backing a plan for a sales campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: Advertising and publicity for a product is its promotion, the same as marketing.

clue.text: Prisoner, worn-out and sorry

parts.note: con is slang for a convict, a prisoner
trite means hackneyed, worn out through overuse

explanation.surface: A tired convict feels regret.
explanation.definitionFit: Being contrite means feeling remorse, which is being sorry.

clue.text: Robbery article by newspaper

parts.note: the is the definite article
FT is the Financial Times, a London newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper report about a heist.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing property is robbery in everyday speech, a near-synonym.

clue.text: Melodramatic articles on test involving Conservative

parts.note: the is the definite article
a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: involving means the test word takes the party letter inside it

parts.note: a trial is a test
C is the abbreviation for Conservative, the British political party

explanation.surface: Over-the-top newspaper pieces about a trial of a Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatrical behaviour is exaggerated and showy, just as melodramatic is.

clue.text: Racing around drug trial

indicators.note: around means the racing word goes round the drug letter

parts.note: haring means running very fast, racing
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A drugs trial connected with horse racing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racing' looks like anagram fodder, but its letters cannot make the answer; it gives HARING.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearing is a court session where a case is tried, so a trial.

clue.text: Discover or find yeti, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly means the letters appear in an unexpected order, a reshuffle

explanation.surface: Track down a yeti, to everyone's astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: To identify something is to establish or recognise it, close to discovering what it is.

clue.text: Nothing included in rent to Canadian city

indicators.note: included in means the zero letter goes inside the torn word

parts.note: rent as a past participle means torn
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing is included in the rent for a move to Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' is not money here but the past tense of rend, torn.
explanation.definitionFit: Toronto is the capital of Ontario, Canada's largest city.

clue.text: Story of people crossing a river twice

indicators.note: crossing means the people word spans the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: a nation is a people

indicators.note: twice means the river letter is written two times

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A tale of a tribe fording a river two times.
explanation.definitionFit: A narration is the telling of an account, so story fits as a near-synonym.

clue.text: Perpetually young wife leaves without income

indicators.note: leaves means the wife letter departs from the word

parts.note: wageless means earning no wages, without income

explanation.surface: A spouse with eternal youth walks out on a jobless partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who never seems to grow old is timeless in looks, perpetually young.

clue.text: Initially supercilious, disregard Italian bloke

indicators.note: initially means taking the first letter of the next word

parts.note: to ignore is to disregard

explanation.surface: A haughty start, snubbing a man from Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Signore is the Italian title and word for a man, Mr or sir.

clue.text: Merit of emptied double shot

indicators.note: emptied means the word double loses its inside, leaving its two ends

parts.note: a serve is a shot in tennis

explanation.surface: Deserving a double espresso, minus the coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: To merit something is to be worthy of it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Various penguins, for example, heading for Europe

parts.note: penguins are diving birds, so divers by example

indicators.note: heading for means the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Several penguins are on their way to Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading for' looks like travel but takes the first letter of 'Europe'.
explanation.definitionFit: Diverse means of many kinds, the same as various.

clue.text: Flipping potato, perhaps, and squash

indicators.note: flipping means the tuber word is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: a potato is an example of a tuber

explanation.surface: Tossing a potato, maybe, along with a squash in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squash' looks like a vegetable beside the potato, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebut an argument is to refute it, to squash it.

clue.text: Royal Navy aboard clumsy ship that's overturned and caught fire

indicators.note: aboard means the navy letters go inside the ship
overturned means the ship word is turned upside down, its letters written backwards

parts.note: a tub is a slow, clumsy boat

explanation.surface: Sailors on an unwieldy vessel that capsized and went up in flames.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' turns TUB into BUT, which takes RN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that caught fire has burned, so past tense matches.

clue.text: Bargain revelation

definitions.meaning: something sold very cheaply, a steal
an unintended sign that betrays a secret

explanation.definitionFit: A very cheap item is a giveaway price, and a telltale sign that exposes something is a dead giveaway.

clue.text: Record of gangster meeting tramp

parts.note: Al Capone was the famous Chicago gangster
bum is slang for a tramp, a vagrant

explanation.surface: An account of a mobster encountering a vagrant.
explanation.definitionFit: An LP or disc is a record, and also a scrapbook is a record of memories.

clue.text: Female expected to return for clash

indicators.note: to return means the expected word is written back to front

parts.note: due means expected, as in due to arrive

explanation.surface: A woman due back for a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running bitter quarrel is a clash between families or rivals.

clue.text: Expression of surprise by Blossom, we hear, about new thickener

indicators.note: about means the outer pieces wrap round the new letter

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: we hear says a word is replaced by another sounding the same

parts.note: a blossom is a flower

explanation.surface: Gasping at a flower before a new sauce-thickening ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blossom' looks like the definition, but it is the flower whose sound gives the flour; 'about' means the new letter is held between the surprise word and the flour.
explanation.definitionFit: Maize starch is used in cooking to make sauces thicker, so it is a thickener.

clue.text: Card game not good for newly-wed

indicators.note: not tells us to remove the good letter from the game

parts.note: bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A poor hand at cards for someone just married.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman on her wedding day or just married is a newly-wed.

clue.text: Unusual utensil holding instrument

indicators.note: holding means the words contain the answer inside them, across the word break

explanation.surface: An odd kitchen tool containing a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A lute is a stringed musical instrument, an example of the class.

clue.text: Discourage jeans fabric being reversed and fixed

parts.note: to deter is to discourage

indicators.note: being reversed means the fabric word is written backwards

parts.note: denim is the cloth jeans are made of

explanation.surface: Put off by jeans turned inside out and repaired.
explanation.definitionFit: Fixed as in resolved or settled; a determined course is a fixed one.
